### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via registerSettingsRoutes (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1081e9777e57ec3c786f855f1a15672e1060dc35` — the merge of head `3bb73c0cd18aafe10a918fe30d377a87d44cc334` into base `dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1081e9777e57ec3c786f855f1a15672e1060dc35 && git checkout 1081e9777e57ec3c786f855f1a15672e1060dc35
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594 3bb73c0cd18aafe10a918fe30d377a87d44cc334 && git checkout -B drift-repro dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594 && git merge --no-ff 3bb73c0cd18aafe10a918fe30d377a87d44cc334

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dc93781c1947b53cff50a550ad551e462a464594` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3bb73c0cd18aafe10a918fe30d377a87d44cc334`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23142 (body, triage grade 6137894223, claim 6138137601, the dev's report 6138827602); PR #23171 (its body as edited, its file list, the net diff of the ten files against the merge-base `02bec6ca86`); and the check-runs on this head, polled until every one had completed. Routes stay at function level here, as the card keeps them.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept-set change the diff makes.** On every route `registerSettingsRoutes` mounts (four, equal to `SETTINGS_ROUTE_LEDGER`), a caller whose resolved `SettingsContext` names no `userId` is answered `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` through the family's `sendError` envelope before `SettingsService` is consulted. Before, the family's own capability logic answered that caller: an empty index, a `403 SETTINGS_FORBIDDEN`, or a `404` that told it which namespaces exist. **Right.** ADR-0056 D2 is the `!userId && !isSystem → 401` default; ADR-0138 D2 lists six door classes and three outside-by-construction families, and the settings family is in none of them, so it sits in the "everything else answers 401" set. The card's acceptance text is met as written.

**Exactly the floor: no wider, no narrower.** The door calls the shared `shouldDenyAnonymous` with `userId` and `method` only.
- `isSystem` not passed, so read as false. Vacuous: `SettingsContext` (`settings-service.types.ts`) declares no such field, `verifiedContextFromRequest` (`settings-service-plugin.ts`) never sets one, and `anonymous-deny.ts` itself declares `isSystem` as never set on inbound HTTP. No reachable caller is refused here that the floor would admit. **Right.**
- `path` not passed, so the control-plane exemption in `isAuthGateAllowlisted` is never consulted. On the family's shipped paths this equals the floor (they are not control-plane routes); it is stricter only for a `basePath` a host moves under an allow-listed name, which the pin asserts non-vacuously and refuses. ADR-0138 D2's outside-by-construction list is infrastructure serving no business data; a settings family is not that, so inheriting the exemption would have been the defect. **Right.**
- `method` passed, so the decision's CORS-preflight pass exists in principle; the four handlers are verb-bound registrations (`get` / `put` / `post`), so no preflight request ever reaches the door. Not wider.

**Nothing refused before is admitted now.** Each route's `serve` is its former `try` body and `refuse` its former `catch` arm, text unchanged; the door only adds a refusal ahead of them. Two expressions moved inside the door's `try` (the PUT body unwrap and a route-parameter read); neither can throw on the shapes that reach them, and the only difference would be the route's own `500` arm in place of an unhandled rejection. Not an admission.

**A signed-in caller sees an unchanged answer.** Pinned per route: `200`, `success: true`, and the service receives that caller's own context object (`toBe`, not a copy). The gating a signed-in caller meets (`403 SETTINGS_FORBIDDEN`, the capability-filtered index) is re-pinned from a signed-in caller holding no capability.

**The authorization-store outage relay.** `relayAuthzStoreOutage` is kept, called once from the door's `catch` ahead of `refuse`, scoped to the `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` brand as before, and `settings-routes.authz-outage-relay.test.ts` still drives all four doors. Order relative to the floor: `contextFromRequest` is where the outage is raised and the floor reads what it resolves, so the relay necessarily precedes the floor. An anonymous caller during an outage gets the declared `503`, which discloses store state and no settings value: the #15999 answer, unchanged. **Right.**

**Mounted once.** `mountFamilyRoute` is the family's one door. The census pin captures the routes off a mock `IHttpServer` as the registrar registers them and asserts the count (4), equality with the ledger, and no middleware, so a later route mounted past the door reds the file twice. **Right**, and it is the triage direction (not a per-handler copy).

**Fixture triage, seven files.** (a) Fixtures that modelled a signed-in caller and omitted the id now carry one (`settings-routes.test.ts`, `envelope.conformance.test.ts`, `settings-routes.authz-outage-relay.test.ts`, `settings-crypto-fail-closed.test.ts`, `localization-timezone-help.pin.test.ts`): right, their own comments say they model administrators. (b) Pins of the retired anonymous answers now assert `401` and `UNAUTHENTICATED`: right, those `403` / `404` / empty-list answers were the defect the card names, and the store-level "nothing lands" assertions beside them are kept (`config-change-audit.test.ts`: both ledgers empty; `settings-admission-tenancy-posture.test.ts`: zero setting and audit rows). The tenancy-posture re-judgment (a refused API key resolves to no principal, so it is an anonymous caller) matches `verifiedContextFromRequest`, which hands the family exactly what `resolveAuthzContext` resolved; the file's docblock records the change and the rows it owns are intact. (c) Coverage the anonymous cases carried is re-homed, not dropped: the capability filter and the `403` arm are driven by a signed-in no-capability caller (two new cases, one moved), and the unknown-namespace `404` is reached by a signed-in caller because an anonymous one no longer reaches the lookup. The ablation reconciles arithmetically: of the new file's 30 cases, 20 + 4 + 1 anonymous cases red and 1 + 4 controls green; re-homed pins red 6 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 13; 38 in all, as reported. **Right.**

**Public surface.** No export, option, spec key, error code or response field moves; `SettingsRoutesOptions.contextFromRequest` keeps its type and only its documentation now says what admits a caller. The `@objectstack/core` imports are existing exports (`security/index.ts`). No governed surface in the file list.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-settings: minor`, summary `fix(service-settings)!:`, a `**BREAKING**` banner, and one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with its facts. **Level and markers match what the diff publishes**: an accept-set narrowing of a published registrar's behaviour is BREAKING, and the launch-window convention ships breaking as `minor`, the same grade and disposition the three sibling doors (#22430, #22431, #22432) carried. The body carries the consumer prescription (sign in; a host's own `contextFromRequest` must put the caller's `userId` on the context it returns).

The two gates, read off the check-runs:
- `check-adr-0087-registration` (the `Check Changeset` job, `pr-automation.yml`) reads the CHANGESET. `breakingDeclaration` fires on the `**BREAKING` banner and on the bang summary; a `Clause-②` arm reading `narrowing` would be a third, redundant signal. The marker is present, so the gate is green: `Check Changeset` on this head is success, on its second run, the one started after the body edit.
- `check-changeset-no-major` (same job) reads the PR BODY's line through `readClause2Line`: `no (narrowing)` carries the level axis, the one moved package is graded `minor`, so the verdict is clean. Before the edit, `no` with no arm read `not-declared`, also exit 0. Green either way, and the edited body is the one the recorded run read.
- So the changeset's own `Clause-②: no — it narrows …` needs the `(narrowing)` arm for NEITHER gate. It is still a carrier drift: AGENTS.md says the changeset body carries the PR's `Clause-②` line, the PR's line now names the arm, and all three siblings spelled `no (narrowing)` in the changeset. Not a blocker, because breaking-ness reaches the CHANGELOG reader through the banner and the bang, which are the carriers the gate reads; the next edit of that changeset should add the arm so the two carriers say one thing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0], the arm on the PR body line.** Answered: option A was taken; the body reads `no (narrowing)`, the true direction, judged above. The changeset's line was left as claimed: noted in ②, not blocking.
- **Deviation: the Clause-② line copied verbatim from the claim.** Judged in ②. The claim's line said "narrows" with no arm; the seat corrected the PR carrier and the gate verdicts stand.
- **Deviation: attribution forms.** The commits carry the model-free trailer pair and the PR body ends in the session-URL footer, AGENTS.md's form, rightly preferred over the harness reminder.
- **Deviation: zero label writes; scope held to the claimed surface.** Confirmed from the file list: ten files, all under `.changeset/` and `packages/services/service-settings/src/`.
- **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally.** Left to CI, where `Lint & Repo Gates` and all eight `Lint ·` jobs are success on this head.
- **Out of scope 1: `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx` § HTTP Surface.** Read at the head: it says requests across the boundary are marked `enforced` and meet the manifest's capability gates, and it claims no anonymous access, so it is true and incomplete, as reported. Escalated as a one-sentence docs-only follow-up (the family answers a caller with no session `401` before those gates). A hand-written tree outside the claimed surface; not blocking.
- **Out of scope 2: the dogfood authorization conformance matrix.** Confirmed from `authz-conformance.matrix.ts`'s header: its population is `rest-route-ledger.ts` and `runtime/route-ledger.ts`; the settings family's own ledger (`settings-route-ledger.ts`, four rows) is not read, so this floor is ratcheted by the package-local census pin and by PR #23137's live sweep. ADR-0138 D2 names the matrix as the enforcer and assigns its rows to card E2. Escalated to that card: the matrix's population should take service-owned route ledgers, this family first. Not this card's.
- **Out of scope 3: the ADR-0069 auth-policy gate.** `evaluateAuthGate` has one live caller, the runtime `http-dispatcher.ts`; the settings family is mounted on the raw host `http-server`, so no ADR-0069 gate covers it before or after this PR, while the REST sibling (#22430) met it through `RestServer.enforceAuth`. Pre-existing and family-wide, outside the card's acceptance text, and unmeasured here too (this record ran nothing). Escalated as a `domain:services` card candidate: which raw-host-mounted families a session held by an auth policy reaches, measured on a booted composition. Not blocking.

Check-runs on this head: every one completed. Every gate-carrying run is success (`Lint & Repo Gates`, the eight `Lint ·` jobs, `TypeScript Type Check` and its four `Type Check ·` jobs, `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1/6 to 6/6, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the four claim-consistency checks); the rest are `skipped` by path filter.
